sentences.text: Both Writ Petitions pertain to the property situated in Sy.No.140/2, Nagawara, Bengaluru North Taluk.
Hence, both the writ petitions are clubbed together and heard.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their status in WP No.2092/2023.
3. Certain lands in Sy.No.140/2, Nagawara, Bengaluru North Taluk was acquired for the purpose of Bangalore Metro Rail NC: 2024:KHC:1103 Corporation Limited (for short 'BMRCL').
Respondent No.3 claimed that she is the owner of land measuring about 465.82 square meters of the acquired land and prayed for compensation being granted to her.
General award was passed in this regard.

However, respondent No.3 challenged the same in WP No.5926/2021 and prayed that the consent award to be passed instead of general award and an order came to be passed to that effect in the said writ petition.
Subsequently, respondent No.2 conducted an enquiry and based on the records available, came to the conclusion that respondent No.3 herein is the owner of the property concerned.

Aggrieved by the same the petitioners have preferred WP No.2092/2023 with a prayer to set aside the finding given by the respondent No.2 and respondent No.3 has preferred WP No.7247/2023 with a prayer to issue a writ of mandamus directing respondent No.2 to pass an award under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Act (for short 'KIADB').

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. The case of the petitioners is that, once there is a dispute, the respondent No.2 has to compulsorily refer the matter to Reference Court and cannot decide as to the title of the property.

It is further contended that the petitioners have NC: 2024:KHC:1103 raised a dispute regarding title of the property and respondent No.2 should have referred the matter to the Reference Court and not have passed the impugned order.
On the said ground, it is prayed that the impugned order be set aside and respondent No.2 be directed to deposit the compensation in the Reference Court.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that the petitioners have failed to produce even an iota of evidence before the respondent No.2 to show that they have some title over the property.
It is also submitted that respondent No.3 purchased the property on 14.06.2004 and a copy of the sale deed is produced here.
6. The contention of the respondent No.3 is supported by other respondents and it is prayed that the writ petitions be dismissed.

The petitioners on the other hand relies upon partition deed dated 23.09.1952 and contends that their mother became the owner of the property partitioned by way of the partition deed and after her demise they have inherited the said property.

However, no other document is produced to show that they have any right, title or interest over the NC:
2024:KHC:1103 property concerned.
The execution of the sale deed in favour of respondent No.3 is not disputed.
Further, it is noticed that the petitioners are Muslims by religion and the concept of joint family property does not arise.
If the petitioners have any right, title or interest over the property, they should have approached the Civil Court and got the rights in respect of the property declared.
The document relied on by them even if held to be true and correct, does not confer any right on the petitioners in the absence of any action taken by them on the death of their mother.
It is further submitted that their mother died in the year 1969.
Under the circumstances, it has to be held petitioners have no right, title or interest over the property concerned as of now.

sentences.text: Hence, for the aforementioned reasons, the writ petitions filed by the petitioners are hereby dismissed.

However, it is made clear that the dismissal of the writ petitions does not preclude the petitioners to agitate their rights, if any, in respect of any other property mentioned in the said partition deed in the manner known to law.

Further, in the light of the dismissal of the writ petitions filed by the petitioners, respondent No.2 is directed to consider the representation of respondent No.3 and NC: 2024:KHC:1103 pass an award under Section 29(2) of KIADB Act as expeditiously as possible.
